title: AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations
abstract: arXiv:2610.21624v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Real-world tasks are often complex and noisy, posing substantial challenges for LLM agents. Yet existing evaluations lack a systematic framework for jointly characterizing potential perturbation targets and types. We use this two-dimensional view to conduct a unified study that quantifies the robustness of current frontier models, traces the mechanisms behind perturbation-induced failures, and draws implications for robustness-oriented training. Through controlled evaluations on APEX-Agents and Toolathlon, we find that perturbations consistently degrade performance, while the dominant vulnerabilities vary across task environments. Trajectory-level analysis reveals that agents rarely recognize altered inputs and often propagate corrupted information without verification. translated_title: AgentPerturb：在受控交互扰动下评估LLM智能体的鲁棒性
translated_abstract: 现实世界的任务往往复杂且充满噪声，这给大语言模型（LLM）智能体带来了巨大挑战。然而，现有的评估方法缺乏一个系统性的框架来联合刻画潜在的扰动目标与扰动类型。我们基于这一二维视角开展了一项统一的研究，量化了当前前沿模型的鲁棒性，追踪了扰动引发失败的机制，并得出了面向鲁棒性训练的启示。通过在APEX-Agents和Toolathlon上进行受控评估，我们发现扰动会持续降低模型性能，而主要的脆弱性因任务环境不同而各异。轨迹层面的分析表明，智能体很少能识别被篡改的输入，并且经常在未经验证的情况下传播损坏的信息。一项针对性的成本分析进一步显示，扰动场景下成功的轨迹可能需要显著更多的计算量。
tldr: 该论文提出AgentPerturb框架，通过联合刻画扰动目标与类型的二维视角，系统评估了LLM智能体在受控交互扰动下的鲁棒性，发现扰动一致地降低性能、智能体很少识别被篡改的输入且常未经验证地传播错误信息。
en_tdlr: AgentPerturb provides a systematic two-dimensional framework (perturbation targets and types) for evaluating LLM agent robustness under controlled interaction perturbations, revealing that perturbations consistently degrade performance and agents rarely recognize altered inputs, often propagating corrupted information without verification.
